title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: From late-night pancake feasts served by faculty to the historic Falcon Walk, these traditions define the Bentley University experience in Waltham.

cards.title: Spring Day
cards.subtitle: The Ultimate End-of-Year Celebration
cards.notes: Join thousands of students for a day of food trucks, inflatables, and a major headliner concert at the Bentley Arena before spring finals begin.
cards.short_summary: An annual end-of-semester festival featuring carnival activities and a high-profile concert organized by the Campus Activities Board.
cards.evidence_claim: Spring Day is a popular annual end-of-semester event held each year the weekend before spring finals, featuring food trucks and a headliner concert.
cards.source_title: 8 Bentley Traditions You'll Want to be Part of
cards.access_notes: Open to current Bentley students; wristbands are required for entry to the concert and main activities.

cards.title: Breakfast by Moonlight
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Finals Fuel
cards.notes: Head to the dining hall during finals week to be served pancakes and tater tots by university faculty and staff in this late-night tradition.
cards.short_summary: A late-night breakfast event where faculty and staff serve students during finals week to provide a study break and sustenance.
cards.evidence_claim: Before final exams begin, Bentley's faculty and staff serve a delicious late-night breakfast to students called Breakfast by Moonlight.
cards.source_title: 8 Bentley Traditions You'll Want to be Part of
cards.access_notes: Typically held late at night (around 10:00 PM or later) in the 921 Dining Hall during finals week.

cards.title: Falcon Walk
cards.subtitle: The First March to Convocation
cards.notes: Follow Flex the Falcon and the orientation leaders in a spirited procession across campus to mark the official start of your academic journey.
cards.short_summary: A ceremonial walk for new students led by the mascot and orientation leaders, leading into the annual Convocation ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: Bentley's incoming class is led by the Flex the Falcon mascot during the Falcon Walk tradition as part of orientation.
cards.source_title: 8 Bentley Traditions You'll Want to be Part of
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually in late August or early September during New Student Orientation.

cards.title: Super Bingo
cards.subtitle: High-Stakes Campus Competition
cards.notes: Compete for major prizes like flat-screen TVs and designer tech in this high-energy event that often features pajama-themed nights.
cards.short_summary: A massive, high-energy bingo event attended by over 1,000 students, known for its significant prizes and themed atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: About 1,000 students typically show up for Super Bingo, a high-energy Bentley tradition with themes like pajama night and prizes like flat-screen TVs.
cards.source_title: 8 Bentley Traditions You'll Want to be Part of
cards.access_notes: Held periodically throughout the year in the Bentley Arena or Dana Center.

cards.title: Falcon Weekend
cards.subtitle: Homecoming and Family Reunion
cards.notes: Celebrate Bentley pride with a weekend of football, tailgating at Tailgate Village, and reunions for alumni and families.
cards.short_summary: The university's combined Homecoming, Family Weekend, and Reunion celebration held every fall.
cards.evidence_claim: Falcon Weekend is Bentley's homecoming, family weekend and reunions all wrapped into one, featuring a football game and Tailgate Village.
cards.access_notes: Events are spread across Upper and Lower campus; some specific events require registration or tickets.

cards.title: MLK Breakfast
cards.subtitle: A Legacy of Celebration
cards.notes: Attend this longstanding January tradition that honors Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. through speakers, performances, and community reflection.
cards.short_summary: A tradition dating back to 1986 that has evolved from a dinner into a full day of celebration and learning centered on MLK's principles.
cards.evidence_claim: The MLK Breakfast tradition goes back to 1986 and has evolved into a full day of interactive sessions connected to Dr. King's principles.
cards.source_title: 8 Bentley Traditions You'll Want to be Part of
cards.access_notes: Held annually in January; often a sold-out event requiring advance registration.

cards.title: Senior Toast
cards.subtitle: A Final Salute on the President's Lawn
cards.notes: Gather on the President's lawn before graduation to receive a commemorative champagne flute and toast to your four years at Bentley.
cards.short_summary: A formal toast for graduating seniors held on the university president's lawn during Senior Week.
cards.evidence_claim: The Senior Toast is a tradition on the President's lawn where seniors receive a free champagne flute and toast to their four years.
cards.source_title: A Guide to All Things 'Senior' at Bentley
cards.access_notes: Exclusive to graduating seniors; registration is required in advance.

cards.title: Black United Body Fashion Show
cards.subtitle: Style and Culture on the Runway
cards.notes: Experience one of the most popular cultural events on campus, featuring student models and local designers in a high-production runway show.
cards.short_summary: An annual fashion show hosted by the Black United Body (BUB) that showcases culture and creativity.
cards.evidence_claim: The annual Black United Body fashion show is a signature event that features local designers and student models.
cards.access_notes: Typically held in the Bentley Arena; tickets are required for attendance.

cards.title: The Rock near Slade Hall
cards.subtitle: Campus Reflection Spot
cards.notes: Visit this natural landmark near Slade Hall, a favorite spot for students to gather late at night for deep conversations and stargazing.
cards.short_summary: A large rock formation near Slade Hall that serves as an informal gathering spot and a place for student reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: The big rock near Slade Hall is a favorite hidden spot where students climb up late at night for conversations.
cards.access_notes: Located outdoors near Slade Hall; accessible 24/7 to the campus community.

cards.title: Falcon Fest
cards.subtitle: Flex the Falcon's Birthday Bash
cards.notes: Celebrate the university mascot's birthday on September 30th with cake, games, and campus-wide festivities.
cards.short_summary: An annual celebration held on September 30th to mark the birthday of Flex the Falcon, the university's mascot.
cards.evidence_claim: Flex's birthday is September 30 which is celebrated by students at an event called Falcon Fest.
cards.access_notes: Held annually on or around September 30th, typically in the Student Center or on the greenspace.
